**Finding submitted: `missing` (TRANSITION), confidence 0.72.**

What I found:

- **Art. XIV runs only against us.** Section 14.2(a) obligates Ono to continue Clinical Studies (i), keep distributing during the Wind-down Period (ii), assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (iii), cooperate on transition and give up customer lists/data (iv), grant licenses (v), return/destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (vi), assign trademarks and domains (vii), and assign Sublicensee contracts (viii).
- **No reciprocal obligation on Array.** Nothing requires Array to provide transition assistance to us, to return/delete our Confidential Information or Data (Art. X has no return-or-destroy mechanic at all), or to certify deletion.
- **Supply gap during wind-down.** We must keep distributing under 14.2(a)(ii), but Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival clause, so Array's supply obligations arguably lapse at termination.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new Section 14.2(a)(x) inserted after p0667 — up to six (6) months' transition assistance at Array's then-current rates, continued supply of Materials for as long as we must distribute, return of our Confidential Information and Data within thirty (30) days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — expressly subject to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix) so the existing bargain on Product Data transfer is untouched. Fallback of 90 days' assistance flagged in the comment.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Article XIV addresses termination effects but runs in one direction only: Ono must continue Clinical Studies and distribution during the Wind-down Period, assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals, hand over Data, Ono Know-How and customer data, assign Product Trademarks and domains, and return or destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (14.2(a)(i)-(viii)). There is no obligation anywhere on Array to (i) provide transition assistance to us, (ii) continue supplying Materials while we remain obliged to distribute Product during the Wind-down Period (Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision), or (iii) return, delete or certify deletion of our Confidential Information and Data. Article X contains no return-or-destroy mechanic either. The "Transition" clause at 14.2(a)(iv) is limited to cooperating in transferring the Product back to Array. No usable clause exists for our side, so the rule's clause is missing rather than at the fallback; we have inserted a reciprocal exit provision at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, data return within thirty days, certified deletion thereafter), carved back for Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix).

reasons: The 'missing' classification is contradicted by the cited text: Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ('Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period'), and Article XIV survives under 14.5. A usable transition-assistance obligation running against Array therefore exists, so the comment's statement that 'Array has no obligation to support the transition' misstates the paragraph it is attached to.

Scope creep beyond the playbook position: limb (A) of the insert imposes a new post-termination obligation on Array to 'continue to supply, or secure supply of, Materials in accordance with Article IX'. Neither the preferred/fallback positions nor the model language contemplate a supply-continuity obligation; if Wind-down supply is the real concern it belongs in a supply/survival rule, not bundled into a transition-and-data-return insert. This is not the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Genre/direction mismatch: this is an in-licence in which the licensee (our side) holds and then hands back the licensor's product data by design; there is no vendor-hosted 'Customer Data' to export. The inserted return/deletion mechanic is also expressly subordinated to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix), making it largely self-cancelling and of little negotiating value.

The genuine residual gap - no obligation on Array to return or destroy Ono Confidential Information/Data - is a sub-element short of preferred wording and, on the excerpted (truncated) Article X / 14.5 text, cannot be confirmed as absent document-wide. Under the playbook's classification semantics it should be noted in the rationale (or raised under the confidentiality rule) rather than asserted as a wholly missing transition clause.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

{"sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0493","text":"ARTICLE IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY"},{"id":"p0494","text":"9.1 General."},{"id":"p0495","text":"(a) It is understood that Array procures supplies of Drug Substance and Drug Product (collectively, the \"Materials\") from Subcontractors. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Array shall supply, or secure supply of, Ono's requirements for Materials for the Ono Territory pursuant to one or more supply agreements to be entered into by the Parties as set forth below."},{"id":"p0496","text":"48"},{"id":"p0497","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0498","text":"(b) For purposes of this Article 9, \"Drug Substance\" shall mean active ingredient containing Binimetinib or Encorafenib that is intended to furnish pharmacological activity or other direct effect in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease or to affect the structure or any function of the human body, but does not include intermediates used in the synthesis of such ingredient; and \"Drug Product\" shall mean a finished dosage form containing Drug Substance."},{"id":"p0499","text":"9.2 Related Substance Supply. Upon Ono's written request, Array agrees to supply to Ono from available quantities in its possession (i.e., quantities not otherwise required by Array in its own development and commercialization efforts) certain related materials (e.g., reference standard, internal standard and impurities) necessary for Ono to conduct non-clinical studies, clinical studies, including, but not limited to analytical test method development and/or validation, for regulatory submissions or Commercialization in the Ono Territory, at Array's manufacturing cost or the purchase price of Array from Array's Subcontractors. For clarity, the forgoing supply obligations not apply to materials that are generally commercially available."},{"id":"p0500","text":"9.3 Clinical Supply. The Parties shall establish as soon as practicable following the Effective Date procedures for the supply of Materials to Ono for use in performing Ono's Development activities under Development Plan and any Joint Development Plans that may subsequently be agreed to by the Parties, and the Parties shall enter into a clinical supply agreement and quality agreement within three (3) months of the Effective Date pursuant to which:"},{"id":"p0501","text":"(a) Array shall procure Materials on behalf of and as reasonably requested in writing by Ono, which Materials will be supplied to Ono at transfer price equal to: (i) Array's manufacturing cost to the extent that Array or its Affiliate(s) Manufacture such Materials itself, or (ii) the purchase price paid by Array for such Materials to the extent that Array elects to have such Materials Manufactured by a Subcontractor. The clinical supply agreement shall contain forecasting and ordering procedures (including lead times), product specifications, delivery terms and other customary terms, which terms shall in all cases be consistent with Array's contractual arrangements with its Subcontractors;"},{"id":"p0502","text":"(b) Array may place orders for Materials with its Subcontractors on Ono's behalf, or, subject to Ono and the Subcontractors entering into an agreement or other arrangement therefor, Array shall arrange with such Subcontractors for Ono to place such orders, for shipment to Ono and for Ono to pay for such Materials directly to the particular supplier. Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array."},{"id":"p0503","text":"(c) Array shall use Diligent Efforts to secure for Ono the inspection rights from Array's Subcontractors for Materials. In the event Array is unable to secure such inspection rights from any of its Subcontractors, Array agrees to secure such rights for itself and, if requested by Ono, Array"},{"id":"p0504","text":"49"},{"id":"p0505","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0506","text":"shall exercise such rights, at Ono's expense, on behalf of Ono and fully report the results thereof to Ono."},{"id":"p0507","text":"9.4 Commercial Supply."},{"id":"p0508","text":"(a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials (e.g., Ono's requirements of Drug Substance or Ono's requirements of Drug Product of a particular Product) related to any Product for the Ono Territory. Promptly following Ono's request, Array shall transfer, or cause to be transferred, to Ono or such Subcontractor all Array's Know-How that is necessary, useful or actually used for such Manufacture, packaging and/ or testing and release of Materials (and the cost of such transfer of Array Know-How shall be borne by Ono), and shall make personnel of Array reasonably available to assist Ono and/or its contractor in implementing the Array Know-How necessary to Manufacture and/or control and release such Materials. Upon completion of the technology transfer enabling Ono to Manufacture the Materials for the Ono Territory under the Marketing Approval, Array's supply obligations under Sections 9.2 and 9.3(b) with respect to such Materials shall terminate and Ono shall assume all supply-related liability with respect to such Materials which it Manufactures or sources from Subcontractor."},{"id":"p0509","text":"(b) Without limiting the foregoing, Ono shall have the right to obtain from Array Ono's commercial requirements of Materials for the Ono Territory. Upon Ono's request, the Parties shall enter into a commercial supply agreement (a \"Supply Agreement\") and commercial quality agreement (a \"Quality Agreement\") on commercially reasonable terms documenting the arrangement pursuant to which:"},{"id":"p0510","text":"(i) Array shall supply Ono's reasonable requirements for Materials for the Ono Territory, which Supply Agreement shall contain forecasting and ordering procedures (including lead times), product specifications, delivery terms and other appropriate provisions mutually acceptable, and any customary terms, which terms shall in all cases be consistent with Array's contractual arrangements with its Subcontractors, and taking into account the regulatory requirements imposed on Ono as the holder of the Marketing Approval."},{"id":"p0511","text":"(ii) Array has made arrangements with Novartis to transfer and validate at no cost to Ono all technology reasonably necessary for the manufacturing and analytical testing of the Materials by [ * ] so that commercial quantities of Materials and can be supplied to Ono and released for the Ono Territory;"},{"id":"p0512","text":"(iii) Materials supplied by Array to Ono for commercial sale of the Products shall be charged to Ono in an amount equal to (A) [ * ] of Array's manufacturing cost to the extent that Array or its"},{"id":"p0513","text":"50"},{"id":"p0514","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0515","text":"Affiliate(s) Manufacture such Materials itself, or (ii) [ * ] of the purchase price paid by Array for such Materials to the extent that Array elects to have such Materials Manufactured by a Subcontractor."},{"id":"p0516","text":"9.5 Limitation; Manufacturing by Ono. Array shall (a) cooperate fully with Ono to make available for the benefit of Ono the benefits of Array's supply agreements and/or arrangements with its Third Party suppliers of Materials, and (b) administer such agreements or arrangements diligently and pursue its rights and remedies thereunder."},{"id":"p0517","text":"9.6 Companion Diagnostics. Array shall use Diligent Efforts to make available in the Ono Territory any Companion Diagnostic developed by or on behalf of Array for use with one or more Products."},{"id":"p0518","text":"(a) Existing Clinical Studies. It is understood that Array is contracting or has contracted with Third Parties to develop Companion Diagnostics (i) for use with Binimetinib for the treatment of NRAS melanoma and (ii) for use with Binimetinib and Encorafenib for the treatment of BRAF melanoma. The Parties shall discuss and agree on the strategy to ensure such Third Party contractor makes such Companion Diagnostics available with respect to the Development, the registration and the Commercialization of the relevant Product(s) in such Indications in countries where the relevant Product will be Commercialized. In the event such Third Party contractor(s) fails to commercialize or ceases commercialization of a Companion Diagnostic subject to this Section 9.6(a), Array shall cooperate with Ono either to obtain from such Third Party contractor(s) quantities of such Companion Diagnostic to supply Ono's reasonable requirements for the Ono Territory or enable Ono to conclude appropriate agreements with such Third Party contractor for commercialization of such Companion Diagnostics in the Ono Territory."},{"id":"p0519","text":"(b) Other. It is anticipated that the development of any necessary Companion Diagnostics for use with the Products will be outsourced to Subcontractor(s) by Array. The Parties shall discuss and agree on the strategy to ensure such Subcontractor makes such Companion Diagnostics available with respect to the Development, the registration and the Commercialization of the relevant Product(s) in the Ono Territory. In the event such Subcontractor(s) fails to commercialize or ceases commercialization of a Companion Diagnostic subject to this Section 9.6(b), Array shall cooperate with Ono either to obtain from such Third Party contractor(s) quantities of such Companion Diagnostic to supply Ono's reasonable requirements at the cost charged by the Third Party contractor to Array plus any other documented out-of-pocket costs and reasonable internal costs actually incurred by Array directly in procuring such Companion Diagnostic or enable Ono to conclude appropriate agreements with such Subcontractor for commercialization of such Companion Diagnostics in the Ono Territory."}]}

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall not include information that, in each case as demonstrated by written documentation:"},{"id":"p0524","text":"(a) was already known to the receiving Party, other than under an obligation of confidentiality, at the time of disclosure, or was developed by the receiving Party prior to disclosure by the disclosing Party;"},{"id":"p0525","text":"(b) was generally available to the public or otherwise part of the public domain at the time of its disclosure to the receiving Party;"},{"id":"p0526","text":"(c) became generally available to the public or otherwise part of the public domain after its disclosure to the receiving Party, and other than through any act or omission of the receiving Party in breach of this Agreement;"},{"id":"p0527","text":"(d) was subsequently lawfully disclosed to the receiving Party on a non-confidential basis by a person other than the disclosing Party, and who did not directly or indirectly receive such information from disclosing Party; or"},{"id":"p0528","text":"(e) is developed by the receiving Party without use of or reference to any information or materials disclosed by the disclosing Party."},{"id":"p0529","text":"The Parties agree that Data generated in the course of performing any Joint Development Plan shall be deemed Confidential Information of both Ono and Array."},{"id":"p0530","text":"10.2 Permitted Uses; Disclosures. If a receiving Party is required by Law, regulations or guidances to make any such disclosure of the disclosing Party's Confidential Information, to the extent it may legally do so, it will give notice to the disclosing Party of such disclosure as far in advance as is practicable and, save to the extent inappropriate in the"},{"id":"p0532","text":"52"},{"id":"p0533","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0534","text":"case of patent applications or otherwise, shall use Diligent Efforts to secure confidential treatment of such Confidential Information of the disclosing Party prior to its disclosure (whether through protective orders or otherwise). For any other disclosures of the other Party's Confidential Information, including:"},{"id":"p0535","text":"(i) in case of Array, its Affiliates, subcontractors, licensees, and Third Party Partners, (ii) in case of Ono, its Affiliates, Sublicensees and Subcontractors and (iii) in case of either Party, other Third Parties as above, a Party shall ensure that the recipient thereof is bound by a written confidentiality agreement as materially protective of such Confidential Information and the disclosing Party as this Article 10, it being however understood that, notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the case of disclosures made to academic clinical trial sites and investigators, CROs, and other Third Parties involved in the Development of the Product or Companion Diagnostic, the duration and of the confidentiality and non-use obligations provided in a Party's agreement with such academic clinical trial sites and investigators, CROs, and/or other Third Parties may be less than the duration and of the confidentiality and non-use obligations in this Agreement so long as (A) they have a duration of at least five (5) years from the date of first disclosure of such information to such institutions, investigators, CROs, and other Third Parties, and (B) the receiving Party uses Diligent Efforts to limit the amount of information disclosed to such institutions, investigators, CROs, and other Third Parties."},{"id":"p0536","text":"For clarity, it is understood that Array may use and disclose, in accordance with the foregoing, Ono Know-How provided to Array by Ono, and that Ono may use and disclose, in accordance with the foregoing, Array Know-How provided to Ono by Array in each case to the extent reasonably necessary for the Development, Commercialization and/or Manufacturing of the Product for such Party's Territory, subject to the requirements of Sections 10.3, 10.4, 10.5 and 10.7."},{"id":"p0537","text":"10.3 Confidential Terms. Each Party agrees not to disclose to any Third Party the terms of this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto, except each Party may disclose the terms of this Agreement:"},{"id":"p0538","text":"(a) to advisors (including financial advisors, attorneys and accountants), actual or potential acquisition partners or private investors, and others on a need to know basis, in each case under appropriate confidentiality provisions substantially equivalent to those in this Agreement; or (b) to the extent necessary to comply with applicable Laws and court orders, including securities Laws, regulations or guidances; provided that in the case of paragraph (b) the disclosing Party shall promptly notify the other Party and (other than in the case where such disclosure is necessary, in the reasonable opinion of the disclosing Party's legal counsel, to comply with securities Laws, regulations or guidances) allow the other Party a reasonable opportunity to review the proposed disclosure and oppose with the body initiating the process and, to the extent allowable by Law, to seek limitations on the portion of the Agreement that is required to be disclosed. In addition, with respect of the required disclosure of a redacted version of this Agreement pursuant to applicable securities Laws, regulations or guidance, the disclosing Party shall provide the other Party with a draft of any disclosure it intends to issue at least fifteen (15) Business Days in advance and take into account the other Party's reasonable comments."},{"id":"p0539","text":"53"},{"id":"p0540","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0541","text":"10.4 Scientific Papers. Each Party through the JDRC or its designee shall provide to the other, prior to submission for publication, a draft of any articles and papers containing Confidential Information or concerning a Product which have been prepared by or on behalf of such Party (or by a Clinical Study site contracted by such Party as sponsor of the relevant Clinical Study) (each a \"Scientific Paper\") to be published in indexed medical and scientific journals and similar publications (\"Medical Journals\"). Commencing with the receipt of such draft Scientific Paper, the receiving Party shall have fifteen (15) Business Days to notify the sending Party of its observations and suggestions with respect thereto (it being understood that, during such fifteen (15) Business Days period, no submission for publication thereof shall take place) and the Parties shall discuss these observations and suggestions."},{"id":"p0542","text":"The Party proposing to publish such Scientific Paper shall, in good faith, consider the comments made by the other Party, particularly if disclosure may be prejudicial to the other Party's opportunity to obtain any Patent. The other Party may require that the publication be suspended for a period of time not exceeding sixty (60) days if a Patent may be filed using the Data or Know How covered in the proposed publication. Neither Party will publish or present any Confidential Information of the other Party without such other Party's prior written consent. The sending Party shall provide to the Receiving Party copies of any final Scientific Paper accepted by a Medical Journal, within ten (10) Business Days after the approval thereof (upon availability and distribution of such information assuming that providing such information is acceptable taking into consideration the publishers' need to comply with any healthcare compliance guidelines)."},{"id":"p0543","text":"To enable free exchange of copyrighted material between the Parties, each Party agrees that it has or shall (i) obtain and maintain, at its own expense, an annual copyright license or equivalent license from the copyright clearance center and (ii) list the other Party as a collaborator in an agreement with the copyright clearance center if required by such agreement."},{"id":"p0544","text":"10.5 Abstracts, Posters and Slide Decks. If a Party (or a Clinical Study site contracted by such Party as sponsor of the relevant Clinical Study) intends to present findings with respect to a Product at symposia or other meetings of healthcare professionals, or international and/or US, European or Japanese congresses, conferences or meetings organized by a professional society or organization (any such occasion, a \"Scientific Meeting\"), such Party through the JDRC or its designee shall provide to the other Party, within ten (10) days prior to submission or presentation, as the case may be, copies of (i) all abstracts that will be submitted for publication (ii) all draft slide presentations for use in oral presentations, and (iii) all posters that will be presented at such Scientific Meeting, in each case, concerning the Product which have been prepared by or on behalf of one of the Parties, for submission or presentation. Commencing with the receipt of any such abstract, draft slide presentation or poster, the receiving Party shall have ten (10) days to inform the sending Party of its observations and suggestions with respect thereto (it being understood that, during such review period, as applicable, no submission or presentation thereof shall take place) and the Parties shall discuss these observations and suggestions. The Party proposing to publish such an abstract or make such a presentation shall, in good faith, consider the comments made by the other Party, particularly if disclosure may be prejudicial to"},{"id":"p0545","text":"54"},{"id":"p0546","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0547","text":"the other Party's opportunity to obtain a Patent. The other Party may require that the abstract or presentation be suspended for a period of time not exceeding sixty (60) days if a Patent may be filed using the Data or Know-How covered in the proposed abstract or presentation. A Party shall not publish or present any Confidential Information of the other Party without such other Party's prior written consent. input.summary: Insert reciprocal Array transition-assistance, continued-supply and return-of-Ono-data obligations in Section 14.2(a)
input.comment: [Playbook] Article XIV only runs one way: we transfer studies, Regulatory Filings, Data, trademarks and materials to Array, but Array has no obligation to support the transition, to keep supplying Materials while we are required to keep distributing during the Wind-down Period, or to return or destroy our Confidential Information and Data. We have added a reciprocal exit clause (transition assistance for up to six months at Array's then-current rates, return of our data within thirty days and certified destruction thereafter), preserving Array's retained rights under Sections 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix); we can discuss a 90-day assistance period as a fallback.

input.quote: (vi) Return of Materials. Within ninety (90) days after the end of the Wind-down Period, upon request by Array, Ono shall either deliver to Array or destroy all tangible items comprising, bearing or containing trademarks of Array (including the Product Trademarks), trade names, patents, copyrights, designs, drawings, formulas or other Data, photographs, samples, literature, sales and promotional aids ("Product Materials") and Confidential Information of Array, that is in Ono's possession, subject to Ono's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes.
input.rationale: Article XIV addresses termination effects but runs in one direction only: Ono must continue Clinical Studies and distribution during the Wind-down Period, assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals, hand over Data, Ono Know-How and customer data, assign Product Trademarks and domains, and return or destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (14.2(a)(i)-(viii)). There is no obligation anywhere on Array to (i) provide transition assistance to us, (ii) continue supplying Materials while we remain obliged to distribute Product during the Wind-down Period (Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision), or (iii) return, delete or certify deletion of our Confidential Information and Data. Article X contains no return-or-destroy mechanic either. The "Transition" clause at 14.2(a)(iv) is limited to cooperating in transferring the Product back to Array. No usable clause exists for our side, so the rule's clause is missing rather than at the fallback; we have inserted a reciprocal exit provision at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, data return within thirty days, certified deletion thereafter), carved back for Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix).

content.text:
**Finding submitted: `missing` (TRANSITION), confidence 0.72.**

What I found:

- **Art. XIV runs only against us.** Section 14.2(a) obligates Ono to continue Clinical Studies (i), keep distributing during the Wind-down Period (ii), assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (iii), cooperate on transition and give up customer lists/data (iv), grant licenses (v), return/destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (vi), assign trademarks and domains (vii), and assign Sublicensee contracts (viii).
- **No reciprocal obligation on Array.** Nothing requires Array to provide transition assistance to us, to return/delete our Confidential Information or Data (Art. X has no return-or-destroy mechanic at all), or to certify deletion.
- **Supply gap during wind-down.** We must keep distributing under 14.2(a)(ii), but Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival clause, so Array's supply obligations arguably lapse at termination.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new Section 14.2(a)(x) inserted after p0667 — up to six (6) months' transition assistance at Array's then-current rates, continued supply of Materials for as long as we must distribute, return of our Confidential Information and Data within thirty (30) days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — expressly subject to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix) so the existing bargain on Product Data transfer is untouched. Fallback of 90 days' assistance flagged in the comment.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: The 'missing' classification is contradicted by the cited text: Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ('Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period'), and Article XIV survives under 14.5. A usable transition-assistance obligation running against Array therefore exists, so the comment's statement that 'Array has no obligation to support the transition' misstates the paragraph it is attached to.; Scope creep beyond the playbook position: limb (A) of the insert imposes a new post-termination obligation on Array to 'continue to supply, or secure supply of, Materials in accordance with Article IX'. Neither the preferred/fallback positions nor the model language contemplate a supply-continuity obligation; if Wind-down supply is the real concern it belongs in a supply/survival rule, not bundled into a transition-and-data-return insert. This is not the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.; Genre/direction mismatch: this is an in-licence in which the licensee (our side) holds and then hands back the licensor's product data by design; there is no vendor-hosted 'Customer Data' to export. The inserted return/deletion mechanic is also expressly subordinated to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix), making it largely self-cancelling and of little negotiating value.; The genuine residual gap - no obligation on Array to return or destroy Ono Confidential Information/Data - is a sub-element short of preferred wording and, on the excerpted (truncated) Article X / 14.5 text, cannot be confirmed as absent document-wide. Under the playbook's classification semantics it should be noted in the rationale (or raised under the confidentiality rule) rather than asserted as a wholly missing transition clause.

input.quote: (iv) Transition. Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition in the Development, sale and ongoing marketing, promotion and commercialization of the Product in the Ono Territory during the Wind-down Period and to conduct in an expeditious manner any activities to be conducted under this Section 14.2.
input.rationale: A usable exit/transition regime exists and survives termination, so the rule is satisfied. Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ("Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other ... to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period"), and Article XIV in its entirety survives under Section 14.5, so the cooperation obligation runs against Array as well as us. The Wind-down Period in 14.2(a)(ii) gives a defined, bracketed transition runway keyed to the termination ground, 14.2(a)(iii) and (vi) set out orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings, Data and materials with defined outside dates (assignment consistent with Wind-down obligations; return of materials within ninety (90) days), and cost allocation is expressly addressed in 14.2(a)(i) and (iii) rather than left as an open fee exposure, which answers the planner's concern about assistance being conditioned on extra fees. This is an in-licence, not a hosted service: there is no vendor-held "Customer Data" to export, and by design the licensee holds and hands back the licensor's Product data on termination, so the preferred data-export/deletion mechanic maps only loosely onto this genre. On its material terms the clause sits at or above the fallback. Two sub-elements short of the preferred wording, noted rather than flagged: (a) there is no express obligation on Array to return or destroy Ono Confidential Information and Data with a deletion certificate (14.2(a)(vi) is one-directional), which is better raised under the confidentiality rule; and (b) Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision, so supply continuity during the Wind-down Period is arguably unaddressed - that belongs to a supply/survival rule, not this insert. Neither is material to this rule's fallback, so no redline.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Ono Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.; counterparty is Array BioPharma Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

The expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason shall not release either Party from any liability which, at the time of such expiration or termination, has already accrued to the other Party or which is attributable to a period prior to such expiration or termination, nor will any termination of this Agreement preclude either Party from pursuing all rights and remedies it may have under this Agreement, or at law or in equity, with respect to breach of this Agreement."},{"id":"p0643","text":"14.2 Rights on Termination of Agreement. In case of termination of this Agreement by either Party, this Section 14.2 shall apply:"},{"id":"p0644","text":"(a) Wind-down."},{"id":"p0645","text":"(i) Development."},{"id":"p0646","text":"In the event Ono is the sponsor of or conducting any on-going Clinical Studies of the Product following the date a notice of termination has been issued by Array or Ono, to the extent requested by Array, Ono agrees to: (A) continue to sponsor or conduct any such Clinical Studies in normal course if such Clinical Studies can be completed (i) within [ * ] following the effective date of termination in the case of a termination by Ono pursuant to Section 13.2, or (ii) within [ * ] following the effective date of termination in the case of any other termination of this Agreement by either Party, or (B) promptly transition to Array or its designee such sponsorship or Clinical Studies (or portions thereof) provided that in such case, Array shall take over such studies (i) within [ * ] following the effective date of termination in the case of a termination by Ono pursuant to Section 13.2, or (ii) within [ * ] following the effective date of termination in the case of any other termination of this Agreement by either Party."},{"id":"p0647","text":"In addition, in the event Ono is conducting any on-going pre-clinical studies and/or formulation studies (e.g., stability studies) of the Product, Ono agrees to promptly transition to Array or its designee such pre-clinical studies and/or formulation studies to the extent such transfer is reasonably possible. In the case of a termination by Array pursuant to Section 8.2, 13.3 or 13.4 or by Ono pursuant to Section 13.2, Ono shall be responsible for (1) costs of carrying out the transfers described in this Section 14.2(a)(i), and (2) all costs of on-going Clinical Studies through the termination of the wind-down period (including for clarity, the costs incurred by Array in carrying out any transferred Clinical Studies through the termination of the wind-down period). In all other cases Array shall be responsible for such costs."},{"id":"p0648","text":"Notwithstanding the foregoing, if Ono terminates this Agreement with respect to a Product pursuant to Section 13.5(a), Ono shall not be obligated to continue to sponsor or conduct any Clinical Studies with respect to such Product under Section 14.2(a)(i)(A) above."},{"id":"p0649","text":"(ii) Commercialization. {"sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0493","text":"ARTICLE IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY"},{"id":"p0494","text":"9.1 General."},{"id":"p0495","text":"(a) It is understood that Array procures supplies of Drug Substance and Drug Product (collectively, the \"Materials\") from Subcontractors. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, Array shall supply, or secure supply of, Ono's requirements for Materials for the Ono Territory pursuant to one or more supply agreements to be entered into by the Parties as set forth below."},{"id":"p0496","text":"48"},{"id":"p0497","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0498","text":"(b) For purposes of this Article 9, \"Drug Substance\" shall mean active ingredient containing Binimetinib or Encorafenib that is intended to furnish pharmacological activity or other direct effect in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of disease or to affect the structure or any function of the human body, but does not include intermediates used in the synthesis of such ingredient; and \"Drug Product\" shall mean a finished dosage form containing Drug Substance."},{"id":"p0499","text":"9.2 Related Substance Supply. Upon Ono's written request, Array agrees to supply to Ono from available quantities in its possession (i.e., quantities not otherwise required by Array in its own development and commercialization efforts) certain related materials (e.g., reference standard, internal standard and impurities) necessary for Ono to conduct non-clinical studies, clinical studies, including, but not limited to analytical test method development and/or validation, for regulatory submissions or Commercialization in the Ono Territory, at Array's manufacturing cost or the purchase price of Array from Array's Subcontractors. For clarity, the forgoing supply obligations not apply to materials that are generally commercially available."},{"id":"p0500","text":"9.3 Clinical Supply. The Parties shall establish as soon as practicable following the Effective Date procedures for the supply of Materials to Ono for use in performing Ono's Development activities under Development Plan and any Joint Development Plans that may subsequently be agreed to by the Parties, and the Parties shall enter into a clinical supply agreement and quality agreement within three (3) months of the Effective Date pursuant to which:"},{"id":"p0501","text":"(a) Array shall procure Materials on behalf of and as reasonably requested in writing by Ono, which Materials will be supplied to Ono at transfer price equal to: (i) Array's manufacturing cost to the extent that Array or its Affiliate(s) Manufacture such Materials itself, or (ii) the purchase price paid by Array for such Materials to the extent that Array elects to have such Materials Manufactured by a Subcontractor. The clinical supply agreement shall contain forecasting and ordering procedures (including lead times), product specifications, delivery terms and other customary terms, which terms shall in all cases be consistent with Array's contractual arrangements with its Subcontractors;"},{"id":"p0502","text":"(b) Array may place orders for Materials with its Subcontractors on Ono's behalf, or, subject to Ono and the Subcontractors entering into an agreement or other arrangement therefor, Array shall arrange with such Subcontractors for Ono to place such orders, for shipment to Ono and for Ono to pay for such Materials directly to the particular supplier. Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array."},{"id":"p0503","text":"(c) Array shall use Diligent Efforts to secure for Ono the inspection rights from Array's Subcontractors for Materials. In the event Array is unable to secure such inspection rights from any of its Subcontractors, Array agrees to secure such rights for itself and, if requested by Ono, Array"},{"id":"p0504","text":"49"},{"id":"p0505","text":"[ * ] = Certain confidential information contained in this document, marked by brackets, has been omitted and filed separately with the Securities and Exchange Commission pursuant to Rule 24b-2 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended."},{"id":"p0506","text":"shall exercise such rights, at Ono's expense, on behalf of Ono and fully report the results thereof to Ono."},{"id":"p0507","text":"9.4 Commercial Supply."},{"id":"p0508","text":"(a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials (e.g., Ono's requirements of Drug Substance or Ono's requirements of Drug Product of a particular Product) related to any Product for the Ono Territory. input.comment: [Playbook] Article XIV only runs one way: we transfer studies, Regulatory Filings, Data, trademarks and materials to Array, but Array has no obligation to support the transition, to keep supplying Materials while we are required to keep distributing during the Wind-down Period, or to return or destroy our Confidential Information and Data. input.rationale: Article XIV addresses termination effects but runs in one direction only: Ono must continue Clinical Studies and distribution during the Wind-down Period, assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals, hand over Data, Ono Know-How and customer data, assign Product Trademarks and domains, and return or destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (14.2(a)(i)-(viii)). There is no obligation anywhere on Array to (i) provide transition assistance to us, (ii) continue supplying Materials while we remain obliged to distribute Product during the Wind-down Period (Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision), or (iii) return, delete or certify deletion of our Confidential Information and Data. Article X contains no return-or-destroy mechanic either. The "Transition" clause at 14.2(a)(iv) is limited to cooperating in transferring the Product back to Array. No usable clause exists for our side, so the rule's clause is missing rather than at the fallback; we have inserted a reciprocal exit provision at the preferred position (up to six months' assistance at Array's then-current rates, data return within thirty days, certified deletion thereafter), carved back for Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix).

content.text:
**Finding submitted: `missing` (TRANSITION), confidence 0.72.**

What I found:

- **Art. XIV runs only against us.** Section 14.2(a) obligates Ono to continue Clinical Studies (i), keep distributing during the Wind-down Period (ii), assign Regulatory Filings and Marketing Approvals and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (iii), cooperate on transition and give up customer lists/data (iv), grant licenses (v), return/destroy Array's Confidential Information and Product Materials (vi), assign trademarks and domains (vii), and assign Sublicensee contracts (viii).
- **No reciprocal obligation on Array.** Nothing requires Array to provide transition assistance to us, to return/delete our Confidential Information or Data (Art. X has no return-or-destroy mechanic at all), or to certify deletion.
- **Supply gap during wind-down.** We must keep distributing under 14.2(a)(ii), but Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival clause, so Array's supply obligations arguably lapse at termination.

Redline (validated `ok:true`): new Section 14.2(a)(x) inserted after p0667 — up to six (6) months' transition assistance at Array's then-current rates, continued supply of Materials for as long as we must distribute, return of our Confidential Information and Data within thirty (30) days in a machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter — expressly subject to Array's retained rights under 14.2(a)(iii), (v) and (ix) so the existing bargain on Product Data transfer is untouched. Fallback of 90 days' assistance flagged in the comment.

messages.content:
Verifier feedback: The 'missing' classification is contradicted by the cited text: Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual ('Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period'), and Article XIV survives under 14.5. A usable transition-assistance obligation running against Array therefore exists, so the comment's statement that 'Array has no obligation to support the transition' misstates the paragraph it is attached to.; Scope creep beyond the playbook position: limb (A) of the insert imposes a new post-termination obligation on Array to 'continue to supply, or secure supply of, Materials in accordance with Article IX'. Neither the preferred/fallback positions nor the model language contemplate a supply-continuity obligation; if Wind-down supply is the real concern it belongs in a supply/survival rule, not bundled into a transition-and-data-return insert. This is not the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.; Genre/direction mismatch: this is an in-licence in which the licensee (our side) holds and then hands back the licensor's product data by design; there is no vendor-hosted 'Customer Data' to export. How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

The redline removes the commencement trigger so we may terminate at any time on ninety (90) days' notice — the fallback notice period rather than the preferred 30 days, which is proportionate here given the transition mechanics in Article XIV. Noted but not separately flagged: the notice period in 13.2 is redacted and should be confirmed at 30–90 days; the wind-down/transfer costs allocated to Ono under 14.2(a) and the post-termination Competing Product restriction in Section 8.2 operate as economic consequences of an at-will exit and should be reviewed under the pricing/exclusivity rules rather than double-flagged here.","proposal":"Make Ono's at-will termination right available from the Effective Date on 90 days' notice, rather than only after first commercial sale of both Products.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-9d217c1c","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ IV DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATORY ACTIVITIES","rationale":"There are two audit-type rights binding us. The royalty audit in Section 7.4 (p0481-p0482) sits at or above the fallback: it is limited to once each Calendar Year (and one inspection per quarter), must be conducted by an independent nationally recognised accounting firm reasonably acceptable to us and bound by confidentiality, at reasonable times on reasonable prior written notice, at Array's expense unless an underpayment exceeding the (redacted) threshold is established, with no access to our systems - so we do not redline it (the un-quantified notice period and redacted underpayment percentage are noted only). Section 4.9(a), however, is a separate inspection right that fails the fallback on material terms: Array (not an independent auditor) may enter our facilities and examine our internal procedures and records to verify compliance \"with this Agreement\" with no frequency cap at all, no fixed notice period (\"reasonable advance notice\") and no cost allocation, and we must provide affirmative assistance. Unlimited audits are walk-away territory under this rule, so we propose the minimal insertion of a once-per-twelve-months cap, thirty (30) days' prior written notice and Array's cost, mirroring the mechanics already agreed in Section 7.4.","proposal":"Cap Array's Section 4.9(a) facility inspection right at once per 12 months, on 30 days' prior written notice, at Array's cost","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-1cd68e2a","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 18.3 selects the laws of the State of New York (without conflict-of-law reference and excluding the CISG), which is the playbook's preferred governing law. Disputes are resolved by ICC arbitration under Section 17.3 rather than in New York courts, but the seat mechanic is not adverse to us: as the Japanese party (Ono), we arbitrate at home in Osaka whenever Array commences proceedings, and in New York — an accepted venue — when we commence. There is therefore no exclusive foreign seat in the counterparty's home jurisdiction and no walk-away trigger; Section 17.3(g) also preserves each Party's right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief. The substitution of arbitration for the preferred court venue is a sub-element short of the preferred wording that operates in our favour, so we note it rather than redline it.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-6275b19d","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"Searches for MFN-style language (\"most favorable/favored\", \"no less favorable\", \"best price\", \"match\", \"at least as favorable\") and a read of the payments (Art. VI), payments/books-and-records (Art. VII) and certain covenants (Art. VIII) articles show no undertaking by Ono (our party) to extend to Array any better terms granted to third parties or to match third-party offers. The only comparable-terms language, Section 9.2(b) (p0502), runs in our favour: Array cannot force Ono to order Materials directly from a Subcontractor unless that Subcontractor offers Ono terms as favourable as those extended to Array. This meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer; MFN-type protection in Customer's favour is welcome), so no redline is proposed. Note that Art. VIII does contain exclusivity/non-compete covenants on Ono (Section 8.2), but those are a distinct commercial term and not an MFN/best-terms undertaking.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-8e4c7ef3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ IX PRODUCT MANUFACTURING AND SUPPLY","rationale":"The supply architecture in Article IX meets our preferred position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, binding minimum forecast, or shortfall penalty on Ono. Section 9.4(a) expressly gives Ono the right \"but not the obligation\" to Manufacture (or have a Subcontractor Manufacture) its own requirements, and Section 9.4(b) gives Ono the \"right to obtain\" commercial requirements from Array — Array's supply duty (9.4(b)(i)) runs one way in our favour, covering \"Ono's reasonable requirements\". The only \"shortfall\" reference (p0430) is a year-end royalty reconciliation true-up, which is the true-up mechanic the playbook prefers, not a volume penalty. Ono's diligence duties (Sections 5.1(b)(iii), 8.1(a)) are Diligent Efforts commercialization standards, not volume commitments. The Section 8.2 exclusivity-of-efforts covenant is a competing-product restriction, mutual in scope, and is addressed under the exclusivity rule rather than double-flagged here. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-2e33f10d","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"employ or engage\", \"hire\", \"no-hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\" and \"personnel\" return no employee non-solicitation or no-hire restriction anywhere in the Agreement. Article VIII (Certain Covenants) contains only diligence, conflict-of-interest and product exclusivity covenants (Sections 8.1-8.2), and the General Provisions block contains no hiring restriction. The Agreement therefore sits at our preferred position under NOSOLICIT — no non-solicit binds Ono. The Section 8.2 product exclusivity covenant is a commercial non-compete on Competing Products, not a personnel restriction, and is outside the scope of this rule (any concern with it belongs under the exclusivity/non-compete rule, not here). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-6aba8729","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"There is no auto-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement: a document-wide search for \"renew\"/\"automatically renew\" returns only patent-term renewals and Section 14.4 (which expressly says post-expiry dealings are not a renewal or extension). Section 13.1 is expiry-based rather than renewal-based — the term runs on a Product-by-Product, country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Term (defined in Section 1.55 as a finite period keyed off expiry of the Initial Royalty Term) expires, with no evergreen extension, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price uplift. The structure also favours us: on expiry Ono's licences convert to perpetual, fully paid-up, royalty-free licences, and Section 13.2 gives Ono a unilateral without-cause termination right on notice. Because none of the risks the rule targets (long non-renewal notice windows, multi-year automatic renewals, uncapped uplifts) are present, the clause satisfies the preferred position by construction and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-f542caa2","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION","rationale":"A usable exit/transition regime exists and survives termination, so the rule is satisfied. Section 14.2(a)(iv) is expressly mutual (\"Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other ... to effect a smooth and orderly transition ... during the Wind-down Period\"), and Article XIV in its entirety survives under Section 14.5, so the cooperation obligation runs against Array as well as us. The Wind-down Period in 14.2(a)(ii) gives a defined, bracketed transition runway keyed to the termination ground, 14.2(a)(iii) and (vi) set out orderly transfer of Regulatory Filings, Data and materials with defined outside dates (assignment consistent with Wind-down obligations; return of materials within ninety (90) days), and cost allocation is expressly addressed in 14.2(a)(i) and (iii) rather than left as an open fee exposure, which answers the planner's concern about assistance being conditioned on extra fees. This is an in-licence, not a hosted service: there is no vendor-held \"Customer Data\" to export, and by design the licensee holds and hands back the licensor's Product data on termination, so the preferred data-export/deletion mechanic maps only loosely onto this genre. On its material terms the clause sits at or above the fallback. Two sub-elements short of the preferred wording, noted rather than flagged: (a) there is no express obligation on Array to return or destroy Ono Confidential Information and Data with a deletion certificate (14.2(a)(vi) is one-directional), which is better raised under the confidentiality rule; and (b) Article IX is not listed in the Section 14.5 survival provision, so supply continuity during the Wind-down Period is arguably unaddressed - that belongs to a supply/survival rule, not this insert. Neither is material to this rule's fallback, so no redline.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-warranty-5f6963da","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"REPRESENTATIONS, WARRANTIES AND COVENANTS","rationale":"Article 15 contains only Effective-Date representations (IP title, no litigation, past regulatory compliance) and forward covenants (no debarment, anti-bribery); Array gives no warranty that its performance under the Agreement will meet professional/industry standards on an ongoing basis and no warranty that the Materials it supplies under Article 9 will conform to specifications or GMP, and there is no repair/replace/refund remedy anywhere. Section 15.4 then disclaims all implied warranties, including merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose, so Ono is left effectively taking supplied Materials \"as is\" — walk-away territory under the rule and well short of even the fallback (90-day conformance warranty with remedy). Article 9 defers specifications to future supply and quality agreements, which is not a present warranty. Redline inserts a new Section 15.4 performance/conformance warranty with a 90-day notice window and a re-perform, replace or refund remedy (plus no-malicious-code and compliance-with-law elements) and renumbers the disclaimer; no carve-out is needed because the disclaimer already opens with \"Except as otherwise expressly set forth in this Agreement\".","proposal":"Insert express performance/conformance warranty for Array with 90-day notice and re-perform, replace or refund remedy; renumber the disclaimer.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-insurance-1dc20117","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS","rationale":"No insurance provision exists anywhere in the Agreement: a document-wide search for \"insurance\" returns only Net Sales deduction and payer references (p0101, p0102), and Article XVI (Indemnification; Recalls, p0715–p0733) and the General Provisions contain no coverage covenant. Array undertakes substantive risk-bearing activities toward Ono — it conducts Clinical Studies (including under Joint Development Plans), manufactures and supplies Product under Article IX, and indemnifies Ono for Products Liability Claims and clinical trial injury under Section 16.2 — so the rule expects an insurance clause and its complete absence sits below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and in walk-away territory for a counterparty performing on-site and data-handling activities. We therefore insert a short Section 16.7 at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, product and clinical trial liability USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Array handles our data, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), adapted to the pharma context and with a self-insurance option; a mutual clause or the fallback limits would also be acceptable.","proposal":"Insert insurance covenant (Section 16.7) requiring Array to maintain CGL, product/clinical trial liability and cyber coverage, with certificates on request.","verification":"pass"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Ono / Array Licence, Development and Supply Agreement

**To:** Deal Team  
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer-side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Array agreement — verified findings only  
**Status:** All findings below carry a "pass" verification (one "repaired") and are drawn solely from the reviewed document.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against our playbook. The commercial architecture is, on balance, favourable to us: the licence grant, IP ownership, assignment/change-of-control, exclusivity and supply provisions, minimum-commitment position, MFN, non-solicitation, renewal and post-termination transition regime all sit at or above our position, and the only liquidated damages provision runs in our favour. Governing law is New York — our preferred choice — with an arbitration seat mechanic that, in practice, keeps us at home in Osaka whenever Array commences proceedings.

Six items require attention, three of them in walk-away territory:

- **Critical — no IP infringement indemnity.** Array's indemnity (Section 16.2) does not cover third-party IP infringement, Section 15.4 disclaims non-infringement, and Section 11.4(a) leaves each Party to defend Infringement Actions at its own expense. As licensee we bear all IP risk on compounds and patents Array controls.
- **Critical — no liability cap.** Section 16.5 excludes consequential damages but contains no aggregate cap anywhere in the Agreement. This is a symmetrical gap rather than an adverse asymmetry, but it fails our fallback.
- **High — no customer termination for convenience until launch.** Our at-will right under Section 13.2 does not arise until after First Commercial Sale of both Products, locking us in through the entire development phase.
- **High — one-sided post-termination non-compete** of unspecified duration on us in Section 8.2, with no carve-outs.
- **Medium — uncapped facility inspection right** in Section 4.9(a) (distinct from the acceptable royalty audit in Section 7.4).
- **Medium — no performance or conformance warranty** from Array, coupled with a full implied-warranty disclaimer, leaving us taking supplied Materials effectively "as is".
- **Low — insurance clause missing entirely**, notwithstanding Array's clinical, manufacturing and supply activities.

---

## 2. Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.2; cf. 15.4, 11.4(a)) | Array's indemnity is limited to its own Territory commercialization, its Clinical Studies and Article 15 breaches; no third-party IP infringement indemnity, non-infringement disclaimed, each Party bears own Infringement Action costs. Fails fallback. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | Patent Prosecution and Enforcement (11.1; 2.1–2.2, 2.6, 4.4, 12.2, 12.6) | We own what our personnel create; no assignment of our IP or Data to Array; exclusive licences with sublicensing rights. Joint Invention restrictions are symmetric and disapplied for the licensed Products; territorial/term limits are the deal bargain. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | General Provisions (18.9, 18.10; cf. 4.5(b)) | Symmetric, with consent-free M&A/successor carve-out for us. Affiliate assignment on consent not unreasonably withheld sits at the fallback. No Array right to terminate or re-price on our Change in Control. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Art. IX Product Manufacturing and Supply (9.1(a), 9.4(a)–(b); cf. 8.2) | No sole-sourcing obligation: manufacture and Array supply are rights, not commitments. Section 8.2 is a mutual, category-limited competing-product covenant, addressed under NONCOMPETE. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Art. XIV Effect of Termination (14.3; cf. Arts. VI, VII, 14.5) | The only LD provision runs in our favour (relief from diligence and reduced royalty on Array failure/data concealment). No termination fee or penalty payable by us; only customary late-payment interest. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | Art. II Grant of Licence (2.1–2.2, 2.6; cf. Arts. XIII, 18.9) | Exclusive Development/Commercialization licences plus worldwide non-exclusive Manufacturing licence, consent-free Affiliate sublicensing, third-party manufacturing permitted; converts to perpetual, royalty-free on expiry. Consent gates on Third Party sublicensees are sub-preferred only. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.5) | Mutual consequential-damages exclusion with indemnity and gross negligence/willful misconduct carve-outs, but **no aggregate monetary cap anywhere** in the Agreement. Fails fallback; symmetrical, so a gap rather than walk-away. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | Art. VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | In-term limb acceptable (mutual, Territory-limited, Commercialization-only, category-specific, with royalty-period exit). Post-termination limb is one-sided, of redacted duration, with no internal-development or acquisition carve-outs. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Term and Termination (13.1–13.2; cf. 13.5, 14.2(a)) | Array has no convenience exit (satisfying that prong), but our at-will right does not arise until after First Commercial Sale of both Products, leaving us locked in through development. Walk-away territory. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Art. IV Development and Regulatory Activities (4.9(a); cf. 7.4) | Royalty audit in 7.4 is at or above fallback (annual, independent firm, Array's cost) — not redlined. Section 4.9(a) allows Array itself to inspect our facilities and records with no frequency cap, no fixed notice and no cost allocation. |
